summary: Robert H. Sharf works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Toronto, Kyoto, and Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and Kenneth J. DeWoskin. He held posts at McMaster, Kyoto, Michigan (1995–2003), and UC Berkeley (~2004).

Robert J. Miller was a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1955–1989) and as a professor at the American Institute of Indian Studies.
Robert J. Topmiller was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Kentucky, where he studied under doctoral supervisor George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini and served as an associate professor at Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1980–2014) and Professor Emeritus at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Tartu, Dorpat, and Humboldt University under Franz Bopp, he served at Ritter- und Domschule zu Reval (~1828–1830), Saint Petersburg State University (~1835–1836), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Robert M. Gimello is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Columbia University (~1968–1976) and held faculty positions at the University of Arizona (~1981–2000) and Harvard University (~2000–2006).

Robert Maclagan was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering, and served as Principal at Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (1847–1860).

Robert Magliola works in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from Princeton (~1966–1970), he held posts at Purdue (1969), Tamkang (1983–1984), Assumption (1985), National Taiwan University (~1989–2003), and Columbia (2002–2011).

Robert Mayer works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bristol and Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen. He joined the Oriental Studies faculty at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1843–1867).

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, T. S. Srinivasa Sastri, and S. D. Joshi. He has held a professorship at UC Berkeley from ~1971.

Robert P. Scharlemann was a religious studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University, and held posts at the University of Southern California (~1963–1966), University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and University of Virginia (~1981–2004).

Robert S. Ellwood was a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held a post at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist. He completed his studies at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1970–1978), later holding professorships at the University of Chicago (~1977–2005) and Yale University (~2005).

Robert S. P. Beekes was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He studied at Leiden University (~1955–1969) under F. B. J. Kuiper, and later held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973, 1979).
Robert Sewell was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and was the Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.

Robert Seymour Conway was a linguistics scholar who studied at the City of London School (~1878–1883). He held academic posts at Newnham College (~1888–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Robert Warren Clark is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang and adviser K. L. Seshagiri Rao (attested 1994).

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930), and as Leiter at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
